payload.question_text: A vendor sends the same standardized invoice form daily. The specialist sees the same labels and positions each time. Which approach best fits?

options.rationale: Machine learning learns from examples across documents. A fixed form already supports simpler explicit rules.
options.better_fit: Use it when layouts vary and a corpus of examples is available.

feedback.intrinsic: The specialist could add unnecessary model-training work.
feedback.instructional: Repeated labels and positions are strong signals for templates.

options.rationale: Generative extraction uses an LLM to match text to schema fields. The stable layout makes direct template rules the closer fit.
options.better_fit: Use it when an LLM must match changing content to a schema.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow could become more complex than needed.
feedback.instructional: Choose templates when field positions are already known.

options.rationale: Ingestion receives OCR results and metadata. It does not select a method for detecting the fields.
options.better_fit: Use it when receiving OCR text, confidence, position, and layout information.

feedback.intrinsic: The system would have inputs but no detection method.
feedback.instructional: Ingestion supplies input; templates use known labels and positions.

options.rationale: The layout, labels, and positions are stable. Templates fit repeated known forms.

payload.explanation: Correct. The repeated layout strongly favors templates.

payload.question_text: A financial-statement team finds “12345” in two locations and must decide whether each is an account number or another identifier. Which OCR-ingestion details can help? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Bounding boxes give each number a precise page position. Position helps determine what the number represents.
Page location provides context for a value. A number beside an account label can be interpreted differently from one elsewhere.
Reading order connects values with surrounding labels. This can clarify which identifier a number is.
A template is one possible detection approach. It does not replace the available OCR positional metadata.
options.better_fit: Use a manual template for a stable known layout with fixed field positions.

feedback.intrinsic: Useful position and order clues would be ignored.
feedback.instructional: Use OCR metadata such as bounding boxes, page location, and reading order.

payload.explanation: Correct. These details explain where a number occurs and what surrounds it.

Manual templates rely on stable layouts and explicit rules. The varied layouts and available examples support learned methods.

payload.question_text: An expense-claim processor has already read “$42.50” from a receipt. The clerk must save it as Total Amount. Which process should the system use?

options.rationale: OCR can recognize the characters in “$42.50.” It does not decide that the value is Total Amount.
options.better_fit: Use OCR when the receipt image has not yet been converted into text.

feedback.intrinsic: The amount would be readable but not saved in the claim field.
feedback.instructional: After OCR, field extraction assigns a value to its business field.

options.rationale: Templates may help identify values on stable layouts. The immediate task is assigning the recognized amount to Total Amount.
options.better_fit: Use templates when known labels and positions identify fields on repeated forms.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk could focus on layout rules while the value remains unassigned.
feedback.instructional: Field extraction is the process that maps the value to Total Amount.

options.rationale: The amount has already been recognized. Field extraction assigns it the Total Amount business meaning.
Ingestion receives OCR text and metadata. It does not give the amount its business-field meaning.
options.better_fit: Use ingestion to receive raw OCR text, positions, confidence, and layout data.

feedback.intrinsic: The system would have inputs but no assigned Total Amount.
feedback.instructional: Ingestion supplies data; field extraction assigns its business meaning.

payload.explanation: Correct. The amount must be mapped to the Total Amount field.

payload.question_text: An accounts-payable clerk reviews an invoice where “Total:” is directly above “$180.00.” The system must link the amount to the Total field. Which clues can help? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A new OCR scan recognizes text again. The existing label and amount need spatial association instead.
options.better_fit: Use OCR when visual text has not yet been converted into text data.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk could reread the invoice without linking the amount to Total.
feedback.instructional: Use closeness, reading order, and alignment for key-value pairing.

options.rationale: Closeness is part of proximity analysis. A nearby label and amount can be grouped together.
Reading order follows natural text flow. It can connect “Total:” with the amount that follows.
Alignment is a spatial relationship supporting key-value pairing. It gives evidence that a label and value belong together.

payload.explanation: Correct. Nearby position, order, and alignment can pair the label and amount.

payload.question_text: A contract-processing specialist needs an LLM to extract custom payment fields but has only a few examples. Which generative AI method fits?

options.rationale: Few-shot learning uses minimal examples for custom fields. The specialist has only a few examples.

options.better_fit: Use templates when a stable layout has known labels and positions.

feedback.intrinsic: The specialist could need fixed rules instead of using available examples.
feedback.instructional: Few-shot learning is the generative method for custom fields with minimal examples.

options.rationale: Supervised learning trains on labeled datasets with known field locations. Few-shot learning specifically uses minimal examples.
options.better_fit: Use supervised learning when a labeled training dataset is available.

feedback.intrinsic: The specialist could plan a larger training effort than needed.
feedback.instructional: The clue “only a few examples” points to few-shot learning.

options.rationale: Ingestion receives OCR text and metadata. It does not provide a method for extracting custom fields.
options.better_fit: Use ingestion to bring OCR results into a field-extraction workflow.

feedback.intrinsic: The specialist would have inputs but no custom-field method.
feedback.instructional: Ingestion is an input stage; few-shot learning uses the minimal examples.

payload.explanation: Correct. Few-shot learning uses minimal examples for custom fields.
